newsitem.title: USA: Fed to vote Dec 20 on new bank underwriting limit.
newsitem.headline: Fed to vote Dec 20 on new bank underwriting limit.

text.p: The Board of Governors of the U.S. Federal Reserve System will vote Dec. 20 on a proposal to allow banks to increase their bond and stock underwriting activities, the Fed said on Friday.

The board released for public comment in July a proposal to raise the allowable amount of revenue derived from dealing in securities such as stocks and bonds at bank holding company section 20 subsidiaries to 25 percent from the 10 percent currently allowed.
That proposal delighted major banks and the American Bankers Association but was criticized as a step backwards by the Securities Industry Association.
At next week's vote, the Fed could consider the proposal as issued in July or an alternative.

The Fed has already approved several measures to reduce barriers between a bank and its securities dealing affiliate. In October, the Fed allowed a bank to share employees with an affiliate and "cross-market" products offered by the affiliate.

And last month, Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig said his office would begin allowing, on a case-by-case basis, banks it regulates to engage in a wide range of non-banking activities through special subsidiaries.
Congress is also likely to take up the issue next year. An effort to reform the 1933 Glass-Steagall Act that separated banking from other financial activities failed in the last Congress.
